aml.verdict: Probable money laundering — coordinated layering scheme
aml.rationale: Cross-referencing the three IQs, the evidence converges. Fabric IQ establishes, on the real data, a 48-hour layering chain across 4 linked accounts, with ~92% of inflows re-externalised and round amounts inconsistent with declared activity. Work IQ shows the team already flagged these counterparties and that a SAR template is ready. Foundry IQ ties the pattern to the "layering" typology, the EU reporting threshold and a prior SAR resolution. Together, structuring + velocity + rapid re-externalisation corroborate intent to obscure the origin of funds.
findings: Fabric IQ · A→B→C→cash-out chain in <48h across 4 linked accounts
Fabric IQ · 92% of inflows externalised, atypical round amounts
Work IQ · counterparties already flagged by the AML-EMEA team
Foundry IQ · "layering" typology + EU reporting threshold reached
actions: Freeze outbound payments on the account
Open an investigation on the linked accounts
Prepare and file a SAR with the MLRO (human approval)
businessImpact: Faster SAR filing: from ~90 min of investigation to seconds.
Reduced regulatory and fine risk via early layering detection.
Fewer false positives → analyst time reallocated to real cases.

card.verdict: Card fraud highly likely — takeover / impossible travel
card.rationale: Fabric IQ links, live, the e-commerce transaction to a card/IP location mismatch and a velocity spike 4× the baseline, on a device first seen minutes earlier. Work IQ shows the merchant was recently reported and that a chargeback is already logged. Foundry IQ re-scores the event at 0.94 and recalls a 96% confirmed-fraud rate on block + reissue for comparable cases. The geo + velocity + new-device convergence makes fraud the dominant scenario.
findings: Fabric IQ · card/IP geo-mismatch + velocity 4× baseline
Fabric IQ · new device seen 12 min before the transaction
Work IQ · merchant recently reported, chargeback logged
Foundry IQ · 96% confirmed fraud on block + reissue (similar cases)
actions: Block the card and reverse the disputed authorization
Step up authentication on the account
businessImpact: Losses avoided: real-time block before the transaction cascade.
Customer experience preserved via targeted step-up instead of a blanket block.

claim.rationale: Fabric IQ exposes a dense provider–policyholder subgraph (modularity 0.71) with damage-photo hash reuse across several claims. Work IQ surfaces a prior report on the provider and a recommended SIU examiner. Foundry IQ confirms the organised-fraud pattern and recalls that freezing payments to the shared provider dismantled a similar network. Provider concentration + reused evidence point to collusion rather than isolated cases.
findings: Fabric IQ · dense subgraph (modularity 0.71) provider–policyholders
Fabric IQ · damage-photo hash reused across 3 claims
Work IQ · prior report on the provider available
Foundry IQ · precedent resolved by freezing payments to the provider
actions: Freeze payments to the shared provider
Escalate the network to the SIU
businessImpact: Direct savings: fraudulent payouts stopped before payment.
Network dismantled in one pass — SIU ROI.

takeover.rationale: Fabric IQ traces the reset→new-device→new-beneficiary→outbound-wire sequence, with impossible travel (two logins 900 km apart in 20 min). Work IQ has a regional advisory and no travel notification on file. Foundry IQ retrieves the ATO playbook and prior resolutions by freeze + verified reset. The rapid chaining of sensitive changes from a foreign IP signals a takeover.
findings: Fabric IQ · reset → new device → new beneficiary → wire
Fabric IQ · impossible travel (900 km in 20 min)
Work IQ · regional ATO advisory, no travel notice on file
Foundry IQ · ATO playbook + freeze + verified-reset resolutions
actions: Contact the customer through a trusted channel
businessImpact: Customer funds protected by a freeze before externalisation.
Fewer recurring ATO incidents via the reused playbook.
